_note: Batch 6 — nursing homes / skilled nursing. Imported via import-to-airtable.mjs; businesses land review_status=pending, evidence lands publish=true but still needs the publish checkbox verified. Ownership in this sector is deliberately opaque (related-party LLC webs); each business is tied to its best-documented PE owner. Two are 'collapse' cases: HCR ManorCare (Carlyle, ownership_status=former — 2018 bankruptcy, now nonprofit ProMedica) and Genesis (Pinta Capital via ReGen, actively in Chapter 11 as of 2025). All evidence is business-level (no firm tags). NOT included: the industry-level Gupta/NBER mortality study (PE nursing-home ownership tied to ~10% higher short-term mortality) — it can't be attributed to a single firm/business, so it has no honest home in this model.

firms.notes: Former owner of HCR ManorCare (2007–2018). Its LBO ended in the chain's 2018 bankruptcy.
Senior-care-focused PE firm; owner of Consulate Health Care and an earlier (2007) co-owner of Genesis Healthcare.
PE group co-founded by Joel Landau; controls Genesis Healthcare through ReGen Healthcare (~93% equity). Genesis entered Chapter 11 in 2025.
PE firm (Simcha Hyman, Naftali Zanziper) that rolled up ~100 nursing facilities under brands including Accordius Health, Pelican Health and Orchid Cove.

businesses.platform_company: Then the 2nd-largest US nursing-home chain; after Carlyle's LBO collapsed it was acquired out of 2018 bankruptcy by ProMedica (a nonprofit)

evidence.description: Carlyle took HCR ManorCare private in 2007 for $6.3B, three-quarters funded by debt. A 2011 sale-leaseback sold the company's real estate for $6.1B — recouping Carlyle's ~$1.3B equity — but left the chain paying rent it increasingly couldn't afford. It filed for bankruptcy in March 2018.

As ManorCare cut costs and laid off staff, health-code violations rose 26% between 2013 and 2017. State inspectors found residents left unattended — call buttons so poorly staffed that some residents regularly soiled themselves waiting for help to the bathroom (Washington Post investigation).

businesses.platform_company: One of the largest US nursing-home providers, concentrated in Florida

evidence.description: False Claims Act case brought by whistleblower nurse Angela Ruckh: a federal jury found Consulate liable for 'upcoding' — billing Medicare/Medicaid for medically unnecessary and inflated therapy. The judgment reached ~$258M; after appeals and six affiliated entities' bankruptcy filings, DOJ ultimately settled the judgment for $4.5M.

An analysis found a web of related companies made Consulate-owned nursing homes appear 'cash-strapped' — a related-party structure that moves money among affiliates while limiting the operators' apparent ability to pay judgments or invest in care.

businesses.platform_company: ~175 skilled-nursing/assisted-living facilities in 18 states; originally taken private by Formation Capital & JER Partners in 2007; filed Chapter 11 in July 2025 (an insider sale to ReGen/Pinta was rejected by the court in Dec 2025)

evidence.description: $53.6M DOJ settlement (2017): Genesis resolved allegations it billed Medicare/Medicaid for medically unnecessary therapy and hospice services and provided 'grossly substandard' care with inadequate staffing — much of the conduct at acquired operators Skilled Healthcare and Sun Healthcare (2005–2013).

Genesis filed for Chapter 11 in July 2025 with more than $2.3B in debt, threatening care for residents across 18 states. Sens. Warren & Blumenthal and Reps. Goodlander & Welch opened an investigation into the PE-driven bankruptcy's impact on nursing-home and assisted-living residents.

businesses.platform_company: Portopiccolo's nursing-home operating brand (part of a ~100-facility network incl. Pelican Health, Orchid Cove)

evidence.description: Investigative reporting (Axios, The New Yorker, Washington Post) documented steep staffing cuts and declining care after Portopiccolo acquisitions — including a Richmond-area (Henrico) nursing home where deaths doubled following the takeover, and a facility where some shifts had as few as two staff for 72 beds, with residents going days without care.
